### **Job Description and Duties**

**SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY) – SIERRA DISTRICT / TAHOMA**

  
  

This position works under the general direction of the Sierra District Superintendent II. The reporting location is the Sierra District Resources Office at Sugar Pine Point State Park in Tahoma, CA.

  
  

The Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) manages and supervises the District Resource Management Program and staff, including up to 13 professional and technical resource specialists. The position provides leadership and direction across the Forestry, Vegetation, Watershed, and Wildlife programs; coordinates District scientific permits, CEQA review, wildfire management planning, Maximo and project development; administers resource management budgets, Lake Tahoe Environmental Improvement Program funds, grants, and mitigation funds; and oversees equipment and logistical support for the Natural Resources Program. The position serves as the District lead for natural resource management issues, represents the District with partner agencies and organizations, participates on committees and multi-agency projects, assists with planning and management functions, and prepares reports, briefings, and presentations for internal and external audiences. The position also works directly on resource management projects, including aquatic invasive species, prescribed burning, vegetation surveys, special species management, and project review, and may assist with terrestrial and underwater resource projects.

  

Typical working hours are 0800 to 1630, Monday through Friday; however, the incumbent may be required to work nights, weekends, holidays, or irregular hours depending on program needs.
  
  
Travel and driving a State vehicle may be required. This position requires a valid Class C Driver’s License.

Training and Development Assignments may be considered

  

This position is designated as not telework eligible.

The selected candidate is required to submit to a background investigation process utilizing Live Scan fingerprinting prior to appointment.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Join the Environmental Monitoring Program (EMP) as an estuarine scientist! Our long-term monitoring program collects data on water quality and biological (phytoplankton, zooplankton, and benthic invertebrate) communities in the San Francisco Bay-Delta estuary to ensure regulatory compliance with Water Right Decision 1641 (D-1641). In this role, the incumbent will coordinate and serve as crew lead on monthly monitoring surveys aboard research vessels and by vehicle, making sure sampling is done safely and follows standard operating procedures (SOPs). The incumbent will maintain, calibrate, and install field equipment such as YSI EXO2 water quality sondes, and perform basic laboratory analyses. The incumbent will manage and perform post-collection quality control (QC) on water quality and biological data and publish it to open data portals following FAIR data principles. The incumbent will analyze data using statistical tools, visualize trends, and share the results through technical reports, data publications, and oral presentations. The incumbent will review and provide feedback on scientific and technical documents and coordinate with internal and external collaborators and stakeholders to execute special studies on emerging environmental issues in the Bay-Delta.
  
  
**As a permanent-intermittent position, the incumbent may not exceed working 1,500 hours in a calendar year. Permanent-intermittent (PI) employees are eligible to receive benefits after meeting the required work hour criteria and do receive holiday pay on a pro-rated basis.**

jobs.description:
**Job Description:**

At Synectics, we're the leading data management service provider in the environmental industry. Based in Sacramento, CA since 1996, we specialize in web-based solutions for Federal government clients. Our team of scientists and programmers is passionate about revolutionizing our clients' workflows with technology and training. Check out the job details and see why you should join us!

We're hiring for a dynamic position where you'll collaborate with our team, manage environmental data, and support client projects. If you've worked as an Environmental Scientist or Geologist, Laboratory Analyst or Project Manager, Project Coordinator, or in a similar role, this could be the perfect fit for you!

If you're passionate about making a difference and have experience in environmental programs or project management, apply now!

**Responsibilities:**

* **Data Management**: Assist in collecting, identifying, and organizing environmental data and documents.
* **Collaboration**: Work closely with the project team to achieve goals, timelines, and schedules.
* **Coordination**: Track field sampling activities and coordinate with clients and laboratories.
* **Client Interaction**: Host project status meetings with clients to provide updates and gather feedback.
* **Data Analysis**: Aggregate environmental data into databases for analysis and reporting.
* **Training Support**: Support training initiatives through live webinars and video production.

  

**Minimum Qualifications (Required):**

* **Education:** Bachelor of Science from an accredited university in Environmental Science, Geology, Chemistry, or a related discipline.
* **Experience:** At least **1 year of experience** in environmental work, such as field sampling, laboratory analysis, or project management.
* History of managing multiple assignments and projects simultaneously.
* Proven track record of delivering client-focused service and effective communication.
* Experience in data management.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Desire to be part of a dynamic in-office team.

  

**This position will be a great fit for you if you have one of the following experiences:**

* 1 - 3 years of environmental Federal Program experience at an A/E firm
* 1 - 3 years of experience at an accredited laboratory supporting Department of Defense programs
* 1 - 3 years of experience with environmental project management

  

**Why Join Synectics?**

At Synectics, we provide an exciting opportunity to advance your career in a collaborative and supportive environment:

  

* **Career Growth Opportunities:** With over 25 years in the industry, we offer stability, comprehensive training, and clear pathways for professional development.
* **Balanced Time Off:** Enjoy a structured Paid Time Off (PTO) plan, Paid Sick Leave (PSL), and 11 paid federal holidays to help you manage personal and professional commitments.
* **Comprehensive Benefits Package:** Benefit from a 401(k) plan with company matching, robust health insurance (including dental, vision, and life coverage), and resources to support your growth.
* **Impactful Work:** Be part of a team collaborating on meaningful projects for the Department of Defense and other federal clients, making a real difference in the industry.

  

If you’re looking for an exciting role in a company that invests in your future, we’d love for you to join us at Synectics!

There are multiple factors that are considered in determining final pay for a position, including, but not limited to, relevant work experience, skills, number of people reporting to you, certifications and competencies that align to the specified role, geographic location, education and certifications as well as contract provisions regarding labor categories that are specific to the position.

$57,799 - $65,258

**RISK ASSESSMENT SUPERVISOR**

**SCOPE:** Plans, coordinates and directs the Risk Assessment program.

**SUPERVISION:** Receives policy direction from the Contract Administrator. Provides general supervision to assigned Specialists and support staff.

Location / Department: San Fernando Valley / Contract Admin. Risk Assessment

**EXAMPLES OF DUTIE****S:** (These are examples of the types of duties that may be performed. Additional duties may be added.)

* Takes responsibility to represent the agency at quarterly statewide Risk Management, Assessment and Planning (RMAP) meetings with Mission Analytics, the Department of Developmental Services (DDS), and the other Regional Centers across the state.

* Facilitate internal RMAP meetings to ensure that the agency meets regulatory requirements and DDS standards. Facilitate work groups with various departments within the agency to develop standard practices for staff to utilize when receiving various types of special incident reports, to include establishing internal processes and systems of support for the Risk Assessment unit in order to best support Case Management in meeting regulatory requirements.

* Works independently and interdepartmentally to develop a Risk Management & Mitigation Plan which meets DDS requirements. Monitors and evaluates the performance of plan components, ensures timely compliance, adjusts plan as necessary.
* Responsible for the tracking and monitoring of timely completion of special incident reports and closing 30-day reporting/outcomes, as well as agency compliance with Medi-Cal claim reports.
* Ensures coordination and communication with licensing, protective services, and law enforcement agencies relative to investigations. Consults with staff on complex risk assessment issues.
* Supervises SIR follow-up, internal staff and vendor training, and RA program documentation. Reviews SIRs to identify trends and patterns and develops management reports. Identifies Risk Mitigation planning needs and appropriately follows up with staff and teams to monitor follow up and identify trends for training purposes.
* Selects, trains, directs, and evaluates assigned staff.
* Represents the unit and/or agency in risk management related communications and collaboration with DDS, service providers, as well as other community and government agencies.

**EMPLOYMENT GUIDELINES:**

Knowledge: Developmental disabilities, case management, DDS regulations, Lanterman Act, service standards, administrative and direct service provision, quality assurance methods, Regional Center's internal and/or community programs; electronic records management; principles of management and supervision.

Skills: New program development/training, interpretation of regulatory requirements, special incident investigation, information analysis and report development.

Education & Experience: Any combination equivalent to or likely to provide the required knowledge and skills is qualifying. A typical way to obtain knowledge and skills would be a B.A. in a related field, plus five years of related professional experience. A Master's degree in a related field may be substituted for three years of experience.

A valid California Driver's License and transportation, or acceptable substitute, is required for this position.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Join the Environmental Monitoring Program (EMP) as an estuarine scientist! Our long-term monitoring program collects data on water quality and biological (phytoplankton, zooplankton, and benthic invertebrate) communities in the San Francisco Bay-Delta estuary to ensure regulatory compliance with Water Right Decision 1641 (D-1641). In this role, the incumbent will coordinate and serve as crew lead on monthly monitoring surveys aboard research vessels and by vehicle, making sure sampling is done safely and follows standard operating procedures (SOPs). The incumbent will maintain, calibrate, and install field equipment such as YSI EXO2 water quality sondes, and perform basic laboratory analyses. The incumbent will manage and perform post-collection quality control (QC) on water quality and biological data and publish it to open data portals following FAIR data principles. The incumbent will analyze data using statistical tools, visualize trends, and share the results through technical reports, data publications, and oral presentations. The incumbent will review and provide feedback on scientific and technical documents and coordinate with internal and external collaborators and stakeholders to execute special studies on emerging environmental issues in the Bay-Delta.
